::: {.why}
The intended and actual portfolios always differ, and a system that cannot explain the difference is one where a real error hides among the expected ones.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Produce a daily reconciliation report where every difference between intended and actual positions is categorised.
- State what you do when a difference cannot be explained.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build the report in qlib/run/reconcile.py: intended against actual positions and cash, with each difference attributed to a known cause such as a partial fill, a rejected order, a rounding to whole shares, a corporate action, or a fee. Anything left over goes into an unexplained bucket, and that bucket being non-empty is the alert.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Reconcile the cash separately, because it catches different errors: starting cash plus fills plus fees plus dividends should equal ending cash exactly. Any discrepancy here is arithmetic rather than judgement, so the tolerance is a cent rather than a percentage.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Daily reconciliation compares intended against actual positions and cash with every difference attributed to a named cause, and an unexplained residual raises an alert rather than being absorbed.
:::
